title: fix(sessions): isolate native workers from host session imports
body:
Related: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/181432

## What Problem This Solves

Native SQLite session workers load actor creation, host orchestration, and configuration modules they do not need. Every isolate retains its own copy of that import graph.

## User Impact

Existing session operations keep their behavior while loading less host code in native workers. No feature is disabled and no public configuration, schema, protocol, or SDK surface is added. Stable process RSS and latency savings are not yet established.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Separate the existing actor registry and binding reads from actor creation/acquisition. Preserve global registry identity, binding precedence, stale-handle custody, and release ordering.
- Move Goal receipt storage, synchronous session reload, and transcript append into native leaf modules. Keep the existing public SDK facade.
- Prepare routing dependencies for each relevant command, including a Goal command arriving after worker initialization. Keep preparation outside transactions.
- Preserve the original CLI turn/persistence failure if stale fork restoration also fails.

Current head `fb751906e73206984c917e17cc644aa82b642f25`, tree `2c765381b7446075747aaa4ad4aac960dce618f3`, integrates main `c5d77b74ab192b446564a35eda787660727676e2`. The two test conflicts use main's independently repaired SQL counter and worker-profile expectations exactly: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184662 and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184667.

With rename/copy detection disabled: production +908/−814 (net +94), tests/support +386/−129 (net +257), plus two wrapper inventory lines. The production growth establishes native/host ownership boundaries without adding duplicate state or fallback paths.

## Evidence

- Current integrated head: **50/50 tests across five files**, covering initialization/rollback, worker-profile fencing, real Gateway agent deletion/recreation, WeakRef retention, and eager import closures. Local macOS arm64, pinned Bun, Node 26.7.0 launcher.
- Independent P0–P2 review: **scoped-clean**. A separate source-overlap audit found no lost main changes or harmful auto-merge.
- The configured Linux Testbox remained queued; no test/build command ran. Its native allocation is stopped. Local proof does not establish Linux equivalence.
- Private-QA full build reached the declaration-size gate: candidate 5,554,514 bytes, ceiling 5,340,536. Regenerating the same private-QA declarations from main `c5d77b74` with the same installed dependencies produced 5,554,513 bytes and the same failure: inherited baseline excess, candidate +1 byte. The normal build completed runtime/plugin bundling and declaration compilation, then failed with `ENOSPC` while publishing declarations; final build gates remain unverified. No size ceiling was raised.
- All **5/5 real Gateway node-control-plane cases pass locally**, including pairing, invocation, presence, upgrades and rollbacks (155.82 s total). These used the candidate's generated private-QA runtime artifacts; the separate size-gate failure remains recorded above.
- Targeted source/privacy checks and `git diff --check` pass. No private paths or addresses were added.
- Direct Codex contract inspection at `414782450952a196bbb64b1605a458c2531c47b6`: `codex-rs/exec/src/exec_events.rs:10-56` defines thread identity and failed-turn events; `codex-rs/exec/src/lib.rs:990-1050` preserves failed/interrupted turn state through shutdown and exits nonzero. The generic CLI restoration change preserves that original failure as the aggregate cause.

### Remaining qualification

**Current-head CI is green:** https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40449158099 completed successfully at `fb751906e73206984c917e17cc644aa82b642f25`, including the normal build and PostgreSQL conformance. Exact-head [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182156#issuecomment-6379368655) is clean, with no findings or remaining pre-merge actions. Earlier failed runs and local build limitations remain recorded below.

Preceding head `2c203f87` failed Linux CI https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/40318146438 in memory-manager deletion cleanup, one surviving WeakRef, and QA node-control-plane setup. Its actual hosted merge passed 117/117 tests across 15 files locally with temporary diagnostic probes, which were removed; that did not explain the Linux failures.

Main now includes https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184616, a separately reproduced fix preventing new cache-trim writes during memory-manager shutdown. This integration does not claim that fix caused or resolves the preceding hosted deletion failure.

### Historical loaded measurements

Prior-head packaged diagnostics used Node 24.22.1 on macOS arm64, concurrency 2, 32 seeded sessions with 20 × 1,024-character histories, control-plane/history/memory-search probes, and a mock provider paced at 1,000 ms. Each arm verified all turns plus two warmups and fresh samples from all 30 workers.

| Workload | Worker heap MiB, control → candidate | Peak RSS MiB, control → candidate | CPU ms, control → candidate | History p95 ms, control → candidate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 4 turns, control first | 1182.51 → 1107.02 | 2688.53 → 2560.23 | 1217.18 → 1249.46 | 15.53 → 25.63 |
| 40 turns, candidate first | 1176.67 → 1108.87 | 2677.42 → 1939.06 | 8708.90 → 8799.36 | 14.72 → 7.88 |

These are historical diagnostics, **not a current-head RSS percentage or latency claim**. The affected SQLite worker used about 62–63 MiB instead of 88–89 MiB. Aggregate worker heap fell about 68–75 MiB, but much larger RSS variation lacks equivalent heap attribution. Main heap increased in the longer candidate run. The short-run history slowdown did not repeat in reverse order. Earlier package-startup, checkpoint, and readiness qualification failures remain failures.

**Rank-up disposition:** the optional full comparative performance campaign remains deferred. A matched cohort must compare the final integrated head against its corresponding main baseline; this PR claims removal of a demonstrated unnecessary import graph.

## Follow-up

- https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/184598 has landed the separate Cron shared-writer classification import fix; its numeric RSS effect remains unmeasured.
- Gateway transcript commits still reach the host entry-acquisition graph.
- Memory-index transcript statistics remain tracked by https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/181594, still on its explicit performance hold.
- Nine observed transcript-reader isolates accounted for about 342 MiB of heap. Idle retirement exists; no duplicate creation or missing-release leak is established. Small-device sizing must preserve lane ordering while reducing per-isolate cost.
